reason: E2 shows TiO precipitation in a different NbMoTaWVTi alloy processed by MA and SPS, not in TiVNbTa by arc melting, and reports room-temperature strength, not high-temperature performance. E1 concerns a TiVNb alloy without Ta or oxygen doping, showing rapid softening at 1200 °C to ~50 MPa, which contradicts the premise that TiO precipitation will mitigate thermal softening at 1273 K. The cited evidence does not support the key premises about TiO formation, stability, or strengthening in the specific TiVNbTa system at 1273 K.
premises: TiO precipitates can form in refractory high-entropy alloys containing Ti and V under controlled oxygen doping and annealing
TiO precipitates are stable and effective as obstacles to dislocation motion and grain boundary sliding at 1273 K
TiO precipitation strengthening can significantly improve high-temperature strength (30–40% over baseline) in a BCC TiVNbTa alloy
The TiVNbTa alloy can be processed with controlled oxygen addition to achieve a fine, uniform dispersion of nanoscale TiO without unacceptable embrittlement
